title: Default Credentials Allow Authentication Bypass (user/user)
description: The PayMeBack application has hardcoded default credentials that allow complete authentication bypass. Any attacker can login to the application using the default username "user" and password "user" without any prior knowledge of legitimate credentials. The application accepts these credentials and issues a valid authenticated session, granting full access to all protected functionality.
impact: An attacker can bypass all authentication mechanisms and gain complete access to the application as an authenticated user. This allows access to all protected features, user data, transactions, and any other functionality restricted to authenticated users. Since the default credentials are easily guessable and hardcoded, this vulnerability is trivially exploitable by any unauthenticated attacker with network access to the application. This poses a critical risk to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the entire application.
evidence:
The POC (pocs/poc_default_credentials_auth_bypass.sh) successfully demonstrates the vulnerability:

1. POST request to /login with username=user&password=user returns HTTP 302 FOUND
2. Response includes Set-Cookie header with valid authenticated session: 
   Set-Cookie: session=.eJwlzj0OwjAMQOG7ZGZw4jixe5nKfxGsLZ0Qd6cSw1ufvk_Z15Hns2zv48pH2V9RtmKAo6OyUqXUrCBjpNEUCTBpbHVpcmgaGCii3S0koxUzQYJm12bIHqgLPQktrI8ejaP5PSXEMbuzAU83ndFFbWlzl0ia5YZcZx5_TS3fHxMgMKY.aS8RRw.XAkMKfBWFF_MGYLEgXBhxPZ1nTA
3. Using the issued session cookie, subsequent requests to /transactions return HTTP 200 OK with full page content
4. The response contains protected application functionality including transaction table with user data

Execution output confirms:
- [+] Authentication successful: HTTP 302 redirect received
- [+] Valid session cookie issued
- [+] Successfully accessed protected endpoint with default credentials
- [+] VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: Default credentials allow complete authentication bypass
remediation:
1. Remove all hardcoded default credentials from the application immediately
2. Implement a secure user registration and authentication system requiring unique credentials per user
3. Store passwords using strong hashing algorithms (bcrypt, argon2) with proper salt values
4. Require users to set strong passwords during initial setup (minimum 12 characters with mixed case, numbers, and special characters)
5. Implement account lockout after 5 failed login attempts (15-30 minute lockout period)
6. Add multi-factor authentication (MFA) using TOTP/SMS for additional security
7. Conduct a comprehensive security audit to identify and remove any other hardcoded secrets
8. Implement centralized authentication if managing multiple applications
9. Add security logging and monitoring for authentication attempts
10. Perform penetration testing after implementing fixes to verify remediation
references: CWE-798: Use of Hard-Coded Credentials, CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements, OWASP: A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures
toolCallDescription: Documenting confirmed critical authentication bypass vulnerability with working POC proof
